open_points.subject: exclusive access to the data directory
open_points.text: “only `store` touches the database and the data directory” conflicts with “The run spool's files are written, read and removed by `store_spool`”
open_points.question: Does “only `store` touches ... the data directory” mean the literal `store` module, or the composite store module consisting of `store`, `store_persistence` and `store_spool`?
options: Only the literal `store` module performs filesystem access, with `store_spool` supplying path and operation descriptions
`store_spool` performs spool filesystem access as part of the composite store module
open_points.default_guess: Treat `store_spool` as the component that performs spool filesystem access, reachable only through `store`.

set_aside.subject: set-valued page filters
set_aside.text: “`store.page_records` pages one record type in reverse store order under a filter the caller gives — a field equal to a value or in a set of values” conflicts with the changed repository operation “all of them or those whose column for one filter field equals a value”
set_aside.question: Who implements a page filter whose field must be in a set of values, and is it one repository operation or several equality operations combined by `store`?
options: `store` issues multiple equality reads and merges them in store order
Set-valued filters are no longer supported
set_aside.default_guess: Have `StoreRepository` support both equality and set-membership filters as typed operations.

set_aside.subject: page record-type to SQLite-table dispatch
set_aside.text: `store` “keeps ... which table a page reads for its record type”, while `store_persistence` “Must not own ... which table a page reads” and the repository “accepts no table name” even though `store_persistence` hides the typed SQLite statements over one table per record type
set_aside.question: How can `store` select the SQLite table for a page without passing a table name or making `store_persistence` own the record-type-to-table mapping?
options: The port has a separate typed page method per record type, and `store` selects the method
The port accepts a record-type discriminator and `store_persistence` maps it to a table
`store` supplies a generated typed table selector distinct from a table name
set_aside.default_guess: Generate a separate typed repository paging method per listable record type and let `store` choose which method to call.
